fields.meta_title: Consultation Form Builder for Service Businesses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a consultation form that reads each client's answers, books the right kind of first meeting and briefs whoever takes it. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Consultation Form That Prepares Every First Meeting
fields.hero_description: Describe your service and the questions you ask at a first meeting. Emergent builds the consultation form, routes each client by their answers and saves replies to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Consultation Form Should Settle Early
fields.features_subheading: A good first meeting starts with the professional already holding the client's goal and budget.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the service booked

Ask a color client about past dye and a cut client about length, all from one link. Each service shows its own questions, and nobody scrolls past fields that do not apply.
fields.feature_2:
Photos uploaded with the answers

Let clients add a photo of the room or a reference design straight from their phone. Each file is saved with the response, ready to open on the client's record before you meet.
fields.feature_3:
Answers in hand before the meeting

Send the completed answers to whoever takes the meeting, by email or in Slack, ahead of the slot. They walk in knowing the goal and the budget instead of asking for them again.
fields.feature_4:
Routing on the answer that matters

Pick the one answer that changes the meeting, such as budget or project size. The form sends each client to the right person or format and logs the rule that placed them there.
fields.feature_5:
Policies signed on the same form

Add your cancellation and consent policies at the end and capture the client's e-signature under them. The signed copy is stored on the response, dated, beside each answer given.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can take with you

Publish on your own domain, which is included and uses credits, or embed the form in your site. On paid plans, export the code to GitHub and link it to the booking software you use.

fields.tab_content_1:
Any box dye adds a strand test before color

New color clients at Saltmarsh Hair Co. fill in the consultation form when they book, with a photo of their hair now and one of the color they want. Anyone who has used box dye in the past 12 months gets a 15-minute strand test before the appointment. The stylist sees the photos on the client card that morning.
fields.tab_content_2:
Budgets under $20,000 start with a video call

Ivywood Interiors designs kitchens and living rooms. Its consultation form asks for the room and its rough square footage, then the budget and photos. Projects under $20,000 are offered a 45-minute video call. Anything larger books a home visit with Nadia Reyes, the lead designer, who reads the answers first.
fields.tab_content_3:
Past 6 inches, it is the artist's call

Iron Fern Tattoo books flash pieces straight from its consultation form. Clients mark the placement and size and upload a reference image. A custom design wider than 6 inches goes into the artist's review queue instead. When Jonah Pike accepts or declines it, the client gets an email with his answer.
fields.tab_content_4:
Revenue sets which advisor takes the call

Pellham Advisory works with owner-run companies. Before a discovery call, its form asks for annual revenue and the decision the owner is stuck on. Companies under $2 million go to the associate's calendar, and the rest to a partner. An hour before the call, whoever takes it gets the answers by email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Consultation Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what the answers should change before you write the first question.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the decision the form makes
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write questions in the client's words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for photos where words fail
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the routing rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the one thing the answers decide. It might be the length of the slot, the meeting format or the person who takes it. A question that feeds neither that decision nor the meeting itself can come off the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Order the questions the way a client thinks about the job: what they want first, the budget last. Plain wording gets honest answers. "What would you like to change?" gets a better reply than a field labeled "Desired outcome".
fields.howto_step_3_des: A photo of the room as it stands says more than a paragraph about it. Ask for uploads only where the job is visual, and say what the photo should show, such as the full wall or the back of the head.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Budgets under a set amount get a video call and the rest a visit. Base each rule on a single answer where you can. If a client asks why they were offered a call, the rule should take one sentence to explain.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the service, the questions and the routing rule into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the consultation form, the response table and the alert to whoever takes the meeting. Change any question later by describing the edit.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add your policies and a signature
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste the terms clients agree to, such as your cancellation window, and ask for a signature beneath them. Clients read the terms at home before the first meeting, not in the chair, and the signed copy stays on the response.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the link to yourself first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form as a client twice, once on each side of your routing rule. Check that each test reaches the right person and that the email arrives when it should. Delete both test rows before you share the link.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template galleries (Canva, Typeform, Jotform, forms.app), a printable skin care PDF, a paper form sold by the pack and a dictionary entry. Every one of them stops at the blank fields. A consultation form earns its keep in the hours before the meeting: it decides how long the slot needs to be, whether the meeting happens at all, and what the professional reads before the client walks in. This page shows four service businesses using the answers to set up the first meeting, not just to record it.
